question: Should OpenClaw commit to this public plugin-owned external-verification contract, including its three SDK APIs and durable attempt ledger, as the supported core seam for external HITL plugins?
rationale: The patch is an intentional new authorization model and plugin SDK contract; correctness tests cannot decide its long-term API, compatibility, and persistence commitments.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow Gateway-owned contract
options.body: Accept the verifier, completion, and bounded grant-store APIs as the supported seam, subject to rebasing and validating the final merge head.

options.title: Request a smaller core seam
options.body: Keep plugin-specific verification outside core but narrow or redesign the public approval API before any stable SDK commitment is made.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave the canonical request open until an owner can commit to the approval, storage, and deprecation lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow Gateway-owned contract
recommendation.body: Accept the verifier, completion, and bounded grant-store APIs as the supported seam, subject to rebasing and validating the final merge head.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the most complete supplied design and companion-plugin evidence and can clarify the intended contract for the responsible code owners.
